sections.history: Korukkai is a village in Mayiladuthurai district, about 12 km from Mayiladuthurai on the road towards Manalmedu, and it is the modern name of the Thirukkurukkai of the Tevaram hymns. Its temple to Shiva as Veerateeswarar is one of the eight Ashta Veerattanams, the one that remembers Kama dahana, the burning of the god of love. Appar sang the Lord of Thirukkurukkai, and the shrine is counted among the Paadal Petra Sthalams on the northern bank of the Kaveri. It is a separate temple from Vazhuvur, the Veerattanam of the elephant a short way to the south, though the two are sometimes confused in lists; the old Tamil verse that names all eight places Kama at Kurukkai and the elephant at Vazhuvur.
sections.architecture: The temple is a modest Dravidian shrine of the delta, approached past its tank, the Soola Gangai, which lies directly opposite the entrance. The base of the lingam is carved with a lotus. In the mahamandapa stand bronzes of Kamadahana Murthy, six-armed and bearing weapons, with images of Kama and his consort Rati; in the Kamadahana sabha the Lord is shown seated in yoga, one leg folded, with Sanaka and the other sage-sons of Brahma at his feet.
sections.legends: When the demon Tarakasura could be slain only by a son of Shiva, the gods sent Kama, the god of love, to turn the Lord from his deep meditation towards Parvati. Kama loosed his flower-arrows; Shiva opened his third eye, and Kama was burned to ashes. Rati's grief moved the Lord, and tradition says Kama was restored to life, unseen by all but her. A pit some two hundred metres from the temple, called the Vibhuti Kuttai — the pit of sacred ash — is held to be the very place where Kama was burned.
sections.festivals: The great observance is the Kamadahana festival, kept over about ten days with the temple's annual brahmotsavam and the procession of the Pancha Murthis, when the burning of Kama is remembered before the gathered village. Masi Magam is celebrated too, with the Shaiva festivals of the year; confirm dates locally.
sections.experience: Korukkai is a quiet village shrine, and its stillness suits the Lord it honours: Shiva as the yogi whose meditation desire could not break. Pilgrims stand before the six-armed Kamadahana Murthy, walk out to the Vibhuti Kuttai, and go on to the delta's other Veerattanams — Vazhuvur, Thirupariyalur and Thirukkadaiyur — all within an easy drive of Mayiladuthurai.

visit.timings: Open daily in morning and evening sessions with a midday closure, as at most village temples of the delta. Confirm current timings locally before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left outside before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is not permitted inside the sanctum; in the outer corridors, ask the temple staff before taking pictures, especially of rituals and the festival bronzes.
visit.gettingThere: Korukkai lies about 12 km from Mayiladuthurai on the Mayiladuthurai–Manalmedu bus route. Mayiladuthurai is a major railway junction; Tiruchirappalli is the nearest large airport, with Puducherry also within reach by road.
